notes.text: Sear the beef in batches of about ¾ pound. More than that in the pan, and it boils in its own juice.

move.title: Trim, weigh, and sear hard
move.body: Bò lúc lắc, Vietnamese "shaking beef", is sirloin trimmed into even cubes, seared hard, and shaken in the pan with garlic and a savory glaze, then served over watercress with a lime and pepper dip. You'll weigh the trim to see what a cut really gives you.

why.title: Trim and weigh
why.body: Sirloin carries a fat cap and silverskin, the thin, shiny membrane that turns rubbery when cooked. Trimming both, then weighing what's left against what you bought, gives the trim loss. Expect 10 to 15 percent.

why.title: Even cubes
why.body: Cubes of one size reach temperature together. A mix of ¾-inch and 1½-inch pieces means some are gray and dry before others are done.

why.title: Small batches, high heat
why.body: Each cube releases water as it hits the pan. A few at a time, the water flashes off and the beef browns. Too many, the pan cools and the beef simmers.

why.title: Shake, don't stir
why.body: Shaking the pan tumbles the cubes onto new sides without breaking the crust a spoon would scrape off. That's the name of the dish.

wrong.sign: The beef is gray and sitting in liquid
wrong.fix: The pan was crowded or not hot enough. Pour off the liquid, reheat the pan, and sear in smaller batches.
It went in too early. Add it with the butter at the end, off high heat.
Trim the silverskin completely, and pull the beef as soon as it reaches temperature.
Spoon the beef over it just before serving, not before.

choices: A thin membrane that turns rubbery when cooked

choices: The pan stays hot and the water flashes off
So the cubes stay separate in the sauce

substitutions.note: Use 2 teaspoons more soy sauce in place of the fish sauce.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then bring it to a boil with the water in the saucepan. Cover, turn to low, and cook. Rest it off the heat, covered, until serving.
Weigh the sirloin as bought and write it down.
Trim off the fat cap and all the silverskin. Cut the beef into 1-inch cubes.
Weigh the trimmed cubes. Subtract from the bought weight, divide by the bought weight, and note the trim loss.
Mince the garlic. Toss the beef in the bowl with the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, the beef's pepper, half the garlic, and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Wash your hands, the knife, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Cut the red onion into ¾-inch wedges. Slice the tomatoes. Spread the watercress and tomatoes on a platter.
Juice the limes into the small bowl and stir in the dip's salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in the skillet over high heat until it smokes. Add half the beef with the tongs in one layer.
Wash your hands and the tongs.
Sear without moving for 1 minute, then shake the pan to turn the cubes, and sear another 2 minutes.
Move it to the plate. Sear the second batch the same way with the last tablespoon of oil, adding the beef with the clean tongs.
Wash your hands and the tongs.
Return all the beef. Add the onion, the butter, and the rest of the garlic, and shake the pan over medium heat.
Check the largest cube with the thermometer. It needs to read at least 145°F. If not, shake 30 seconds more.
Spoon the beef and onion over the watercress. Serve with the rice and the lime dip on the side.
